newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore says ties with Malaysia normalising.
newsitem.headline: Singapore says ties with Malaysia normalising.

text.p: Singapore-Malaysia relations, which hit a low point after a row in March, are slowly normalising, Singapore Foreign Minister Shanmugam Jayakumar said on Wednesday.
"I believe that the waves appeared to have subsided and things are slowly returning to normal," he told parliament.

The spat between the neighbours began when Singapore Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew said in a court affidavit made public in March that Malaysia's Johor Baru was notorious for shootings, muggings and car-jackings, sparking a heated response from Malaysia.
Lee twice apologised for the remarks, but the issue has rankled.
"Singapore is committed to establish a long term relationship with Malaysia based on mutual respect, trust reciprocity and mutual benefit," Jayakumar said.
Malaysian leaders have said it will take time for relations to return to normal, he said.
"Singapore will do its part to improve ties but we leave it to the Malaysia leaders to set the pace," he said.

He said as a sign that ties are improving, the topping out ceremony of the bridge which is the second link between the two countries will proceed as scheduled on Thursday and it will be officially opened on June 2 next year.
